overclaims: In the same week, CNBC reported that Cursor, Vercel and Factory made GPT-5 their default model, and Box's CEO called it 'unbelievably well' performing (e2, e3).
A contemporaneous report described users as split, not uniformly unhappy (e4).
Consumer backlash was real, but satisfaction was not rare among developer and enterprise customers.
No representative survey exists, so the balance of satisfied and dissatisfied users is inferred from reporting.
Enterprise praise came partly from OpenAI launch partners, who may have had reasons to be positive.
checks.note: Default adoption was limited to certain products/tools. The split concerned comparative performance, not satisfaction. Named positive customers do not establish satisfaction prevalence. No survey was found; nonexistence is unproven. Launch-partner status and suggested motives lack support. The mixed outcome and citation fields match the frozen case.
